report.answer_text:
Tower cranes are standard engineering equipment, so I'm answering from established knowledge and didn't search.
Main Structural Parts
1. Base (Foundation)
A reinforced concrete slab, often with anchor bolts or a fixing angle set into it.
Carries the crane's weight and the loads it lifts, and keeps the crane stable.
2. Mast (Tower)
A lattice steel column made of bolted or pinned sections.
Gives the crane its height. Sections can be added to raise it as the building grows, a process called "climbing" or "jumping."
3. Slewing Unit (Slewing Ring)
Sits at the top of the mast.
Contains the gear and motor that rotate the crane's upper part, usually a full 360°.
4. Operator's Cab
The control station, mounted near the slewing unit.
The operator uses joysticks or pedals to control hoisting, trolley movement and slewing. Many cranes can also be run by remote control.
Horizontal Components
5. Jib (Working Arm)
The long horizontal arm that carries the load out from the mast.
Its length sets the crane's working radius.
6. Counter-Jib (Machinery Arm)
The shorter arm on the opposite side of the mast.
Holds the counterweights, the hoist motor and the electrical gear.
7. Counterweights
Heavy concrete or steel blocks on the counter-jib.
Balance the load on the jib so the crane doesn't tip.
8. Trolley
Runs along the underside of the jib.
Moves the load in and out horizontally, changing the working radius.
Lifting Components
9. Hoist Winch/Motor
Usually on the counter-jib.
Winds the hoist rope in and out to raise and lower loads.
10. Hoist Rope (Wire Rope)
Steel cable that runs from the winch along the jib and through the trolley to the hook block.
11. Hook Block (Hook Assembly)
The pulley block and hook that hang from the trolley.
Attaches to the load through slings or rigging.
Support and Safety Components
12. Tower Head / Apex (A-frame)
The peak above the slewing unit.
Anchors the pendant (tie) bars that support the jib and counter-jib.
13. Pendant Bars (Tie Rods)
Steel ties from the apex to the jib and counter-jib.
Carry tension loads and hold the arms in place.
14. Climbing Frame / Hydraulic Jacking Cage
Used when the crane is extended.
Lifts the upper structure so new mast sections can be inserted.
15. Ties / Anchors (Tie-ins)
Brackets that fix the mast to the building at intervals on very tall installations.
Give extra lateral stability.
16. Safety Devices
Load moment limiter: stops lifting if the load is too heavy for the radius.
Limit switches: restrict hook height, trolley travel and slewing.
Anemometer: measures wind speed to warn of unsafe conditions.
Weathervane (free-slewing) mode: lets the jib turn with the wind when the crane is out of service.
How It Works Together
The operator in the cab moves the trolley along the jib to the right radius. The winch then lowers the hook, and the load is lifted. The slewing unit swings the jib to the drop point. The counterweights balance the load throughout, and the safety systems keep the crane within its rated limits.
I can also explain the types of tower crane (hammerhead, luffing jib, flat-top, self-erecting) or the erection process if that would help.
